text:
laura: Quick follow-up on the regional fairness-window RFC — a couple privacy and cache-churn tradeoffs popped up when I sketched the implementation. Specifically: using client fingerprints to smooth bursts across regions seems effective, but it may expose PII and amplify churn when clients change IPs or rotate devices. Thoughts?

rafael: I like the idea of smoothing, but we should avoid raw identifiers. Proposal: derive ephemeral IDs as a hash of a client token + region salt + epoch. That way we can rotate without revealing original values.

laura: Yeah, something like `client_id = sha256(token + ":" + cluster_id + ":" + epoch)` — keep 3 recent epochs in cache so short rotations don't drop hits. Main questions: how long should epoch be, and how do we rotate salts without cache stampede?

ben: Operationally, cache miss spikes will cause tail latency, especially for large tenants that suddenly land in a new region. We should simulate trace replays to quantify hit-rate vs epoch length. Also consider linear backoff for fallback path to avoid thundering.

maria: Legal/security: hashing device IDs still may be PII depending on jurisdiction. We should prefer client-generated ephemeral tokens in the API and treat any derived hash as pseudonymous data; flag for privacy review.

infra-bot: runbook: queued simulation job `fair-window-sim` (owner: laura) — workload: 100k tenants, geo distribution, churn model v2. Link: https://ci.redwood/sim/1234 :white_check_mark:

laura: Operational fallback I'm proposing: prefer ephemeral client token when present; if absent, fall back to salted hash of IP+user-agent with higher penalty weight. Penalty ensures we don't over-rely on less-stable signals.

megan: How does this change reconciliation semantics between edge proxies and the central quota ledger? If epochs are short, we might see more duplicates during reconcile. Need to pick reconcile window > epoch.

laura: Good catch. Plan: epoch = 10m, reconcile_window = 30m, keep 3 epochs active in caches (current, -1, -2). That should bound churn while keeping IDs reasonably short-lived.

ben: SGTM. Add telemetry for `fair_window_cache_miss`, `fair_window_epoch_rotate`, and `reconcile_retry_rate` so we can alert if miss rate or retries spike after rollout.

maria: I'll start the privacy review and list jurisdictions we need to be careful about (EU, CA). If client token is optional, require docs for SDKs to advertise ephemeral tokens.

laura: Thanks — I'll draft an RFC follow-up with the sim results once `fair-window-sim` finishes and include the exact deploy knobs (epoch, penalty weights, fallback hierarchy). Will also include a short code snippet for derivation and TTL table. :thumbsup:

rafael: Nice. One more operational note — when rotating cluster salts, do a staged rollout: cluster A rotates, clusters B/C accept old+new salts for N minutes to avoid cross-region mismatches.

laura: Agreed — staged salt rotation + migration window. Filing follow-up thread and will attach sim logs.
